mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Commissioner for Oaths in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and UBOs against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, Australian DFAT Consolidated List, New Zealand Sanctions list, and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, requiring senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and supporting AML/CFT guidance issued by SIFA and the Central Bank of Samoa.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Online Registry Portal - International Companies Division, Samoa International Finance Authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Roman script. Samoan-language names are accepted if written with standard Samoan orthography. Foreign names, including Chinese names, may be used as trading names or adopted in the Articles of Association only after a notarized Roman-script transliteration is filed with the Registrar. Full Chinese-language Articles of Association are permissible as internal constitutional documents, provided that an English translation is certified by a Samoan notary public and delivered to the registered agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of rejection, stating the grounds and enclosing authority to use the name. The Registrar must decide within 14 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a revised name without losing the original filing date or may apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days. A reserved name may be extended only once for an additional 30-day period, for a maximum total of 60 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory registered office. The registered office must be a physical address of a licensed International Company Service Provider in Samoa. A virtual office may be used only for non-statutory correspondence and business administration; it cannot satisfy the registered-office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for a cross-border remittance International Company. Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is estimated at 85-90% within the first 12 months if the money transmission license is applied for, due to the high-risk classification. For a non-licensed holding or payment-rail support International Company, the likelihood is an estimated 25-35%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2011; Sections 4 (Incorporation), 7 (Memorandum and Articles), 12 (Registered Office and Agent), and 26 (Directors and Secretary)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association, filed with accompanying Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; applicant may declare nominal share capital (commonly USD 1 split into shares of USD 1 each); no escrow or deposit account required at incorporation; shares may be issued partly paid with board approval
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company adopts its Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of International Companies, and confirms the subscription of one ordinary share by the sole initial subscriber, fully paid in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the registered agent's address in Apia, Samoa, and that the registered agent be appointed in accordance with statutory requirements. RESOLVED, that [Director] be appointed sole Director and [Secretary] be appointed Company Secretary, each to serve until duly replaced. RESOLVED, that the Director is authorized to execute all registrations, engage service providers, and procure the remittance service provider license from the Central Bank of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation request through a licensed SIFA registered agent, stating the proposed corporate name with the mandatory suffix 'Limited' and the intended object of cross-border money transmission. The Registrar will screen the name against the National Companies Register and reject names that are identical, misleading, or prohibited under the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application letter
Identity and authorization letter of the licensed registered agent
Proposed corporate name in English
Brief statement of intended business objects
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a revised application with a new name within 14 days, or appeal in writing to the Registrar for a determination under Section 7(3) of the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent licensed by SIFA (notarial attestation in Apia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, incorporating the reserved name, registered office clause, share capital provisions, director and secretary clauses, and the stated purpose of operating a cross-border remittance and money transmission agency. The sole subscriber and proposed director must execute the documents before the registered agent or a Samoa notary public, with signatures witnessed.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified passport copy of subscriber and proposed director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
Signed consent to act as director
Signed consent to act as company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises deficiencies in the constitutive documents, the registered agent will amend and re-execute the affected clauses within 10 business days and resubmit without new fees, provided the original filing fee remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 and the statutory filing fee of USD 200 through the SIFA online portal or physical counter. The Registrar verifies compliance with the International Companies Act 1987 and issues a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
Name reservation certificate
Consent forms of director, secretary, and registered agent
Filing fee payment receipt (USD 200)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the registered agent files a curative submission with amended documents within 10 business days; any rejection notice must specify the statutory ground, and the applicant may appeal to the Minister for Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Endorsement of Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. The registered agent assembles the corporate kit comprising the certificate, seal, share certificates, and certified copies of the constitutional documents; the kit is then delivered to the client along with the appointment letter for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Corporate stamp and seal
Share certificates for initial subscriber
Register of directors, secretary, and shareholders
Registered office and registered agent appointment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors, the registered agent submits a written rectification request under Section 4(4) of the Act; the Registrar will issue a corrected certificate within 5 business days at no cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (AML/CFT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, Central Bank of Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the AML/CFT registration form as a reporting entity under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, including the company's business plan for cross-border remittance, AML policy, and identification of the Compliance Officer. This registration is a precondition for the specialized remittance license application.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT reporting entity registration form
Business plan for cross-border remittance operations
AML/CFT compliance manual and risk assessment
Identity of designated Compliance Officer
Certificate of Incorporation
Organizational chart of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is deferred, the applicant may submit supplementary risk mitigation documentation within 20 business days or request a formal hearing before the Financial Intelligence Unit; regulatory clarifications are resolved through the licensed registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commencement of Registered Office and Statutory Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent (SIFA-licensed) and Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the registered office at the agent's address in Apia, maintain the statutory registers at the registered office, file the annual return and statement of directors within the first month after incorporation, and confirm the appointment of the registered agent for the first year of operations. The company must display the Certificate of Incorporation at its principal place of business.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, charges)
Annual return filing form
Registered agent annual service fee payment
Oath of compliance by the director
Notice of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any late or defective post-incorporation filing triggers a penalty notice under the Act; the company may lodge an objection with the Registrar, and the registered agent will normalize the filing within 7 business days to mitigate fines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Samoa, Banking Supervision Department (Apia)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Remittance Service Provider License under the Financial Institutions Act 1996 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Money Transmission and Cross-Border Remittance Operating Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa, in coordination with the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-Impact Service Activity – EIA Registration Only (Category B, Schedule 3 of the Planning and Urban Management (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2012); no full EIA report required for office-based remittance operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent anticipated: office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge limits under the Water Resources Management Act 2008; zero VOC or stack emissions; electronic records and e-waste must be disposed through MNRE-approved recyclers; transactional data kept offsite with sealed paper records for 5 years per AML retention rules; noise and lighting limited to Abatement Notice standards for office districts in Apia.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) confirming compliance with fire suppression, emergency egress, and smoke detection requirements; structural load inspection certificate for the leased office premises issued by MCIL Building Inspectorate; workplace occupational safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002, including first-aid provisions, electrical safety, and evacuation drills; Business License Approval from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for commercial premises occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), established under the Samoa Revenue Authority Act 2022; official e-services portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws (legacy Ministry of Revenue gateway: https://www.revenue.gov.ws). The SRA administers the Income Tax Act 2012, the Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) Act 1992, the Tax Administration Act 2012, and excise duties; customs export declarations are filed with the Samoa Customs Service as a separate functional arm of the public revenue system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 through the Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour), appointing a licensed Samoan registered agent. Step 2 - File the prescribed Application for Tax Identification Number (TIN) at the SRA e-Services portal together with the certificate of incorporation, registered agent certificate, authenticated director and shareholder identification, and proof of registered office in Samoa. Step 3 - The SRA issues an 8-digit TIN within 3-5 business days; while the IC remains inactive in Samoa, no domestic income tax registration is required, but a separate VAGST registration is mandatory if taxable supplies in Samoa reach or are likely to reach WST 60,000 per annum. Step 4 - Secure the statutory banking/money-transmission licence from the Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) before operating the cross-border remittance rail; the CBS licence number and SRA TIN are cross-referenced for AML/CFT supervisory data matching.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. The IC is a non-resident company that, under the International Companies Act 1987, is exempt from income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, and withholding taxes on all income, assets, and transactions sourced or carried on outside Samoa, with its only recurring public charge being the annual government fee. Samoa applies a territorial/source-based income tax system under the Income Tax Act 2012; accordingly, if the IC actually carries on business in Samoa (including a physical payout or cash-pickup operation, or services rendered wholly within Samoa), the exemption is forfeited to that extent and the IC becomes liable to corporate income tax on Samoa-source income at the prevailing domestic rate (currently 27%), VAGST at 15%, and applicable PAYE obligations. The tax-exempt classification is therefore not a blanket waiver for in-Samoa activities used to perform the remittance payout leg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no IRC 7701-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid-mismatch regime. Available statutory mechanisms are: (i) under the International Companies Act 1987, an IC may apply to the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) for a special licence authorising a specific domestic transaction, which is the sole elective pathway that voluntarily brings the entity into the domestic tax net; (ii) under the Income Tax Act 2012, qualifying Samoa-source passive income of a non-resident IC is taxed by final withholding at source rather than by assessment, requiring no election; (iii) group relief provisions apply only among resident companies under common control; and (iv) the general anti-avoidance rule and transfer pricing provisions operate to disregard arrangements that artificially mismatch the IC tax-exempt status with the domestic tax system. Conversion of the IC into an ordinary domestic company under the Companies Act 2006 is available and terminates the tax-exempt zone treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 (SAT 60,000) annual taxable turnover of supplies made in Samoa; registration is compulsory when actual or expected taxable supplies in any 12-month period reach the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based tax invoice validation. A tax invoice must be issued within 28 days of supply and state the supplier name and TIN, VAGST registration number, sequential invoice number, issue date, description of the supply, tax amount, and total price; invoices may be paper or electronic. VAGST returns are filed through the SRA e-filing portal on monthly, quarterly, or semi-annual cycles depending on turnover, and taxpayers must retain accounting records for at least 7 years. The SRA conducts data matching against Central Bank of Samoa payment-rail records (SWIFT MT103/MT202 and payout reconciliation files) to verify declared turnover, but no pre-clearance or fiscal stamping obligation is legislated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (i) goods physically exported from Samoa, and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and for use outside Samoa, including services directly connected with export goods or international transport. For the cross-border remittance rail, a fee charged to and paid by the overseas remitter is eligible for zero-rating only if the operator can evidence that the supply was made to the non-resident and that the service is not an exempt financial supply; to the extent a fee is charged to the Samoan beneficiary (cash-pickup or payout commission), that part is a domestic supply and falls under the financial services exemption in Schedule 2 of the VAGST Act, which is exempt rather than zero-rated and blocks input VAT recovery on related costs. Given the overlap, the operator should obtain a binding written ruling from the SRA on the characterisation of each fee type before claiming zero-rating on services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Entry / Export Declaration issued by the Samoa Customs Service (required only for goods export legs)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorised dealer bank or the Central Bank of Samoa for service export substantiation
Commercial invoice and payment settlement evidence (SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages and corresponding bank statements)
Signed service agreement with the non-resident remitter identifying the counterparty jurisdiction and place of performance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA may audit zero-rating claims for up to 5 years, with no time limit in cases of fraud, and may claw back short-paid VAGST together with statutory interest. Under the Tax Administration Act 2012, a false or unsupported zero-rating claim attracts a civil shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax avoided (75% for recklessness) and, upon conviction, fines and imprisonment for responsible individuals; knowingly submitting forged customs documentation or falsified CBS remittance records also exposes the IC to revocation of the money-transmission licence, exclusion from refund credits, and criminal prosecution. VAGST refunds of excess input credits are released only after documentary verification against customs and Central Bank records, and flagged entities may be required to post a bank guarantee until audit clearance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; statutory name: Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), exercising delegated powers under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 1976, and the Exchange Control Regulations 1985
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a statutory exchange-control regime administered by CBS through authorized dealer banks. Current-account items (trade settlement, service fees, family remittances, and documented operating expenses) are normally approved at the authorized-dealer level against full documentary support. Capital-account items (equity injection, offshore borrowing, loan repayment, and investment liquidation) require prior CBS exchange-control approval and are assessed for balance-of-payments and prudential impact. Profit remittance is permissible for an International Company (IC), but the IC is statutorily barred from carrying on business with Samoan residents or deriving domestic-source income under the International Companies Act 1987; consequently, the IC is confined to a non-resident treasury and foreign-currency float role, while all WST-denominated customer-facing settlement must be executed through a separately incorporated, locally licensed remittance agent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1985, proceeds from exports of goods and services, including cross-border remittance aggregation, must be repatriated to Samoa within 6 months (180 days) of the date the amount becomes receivable and, unless CBS has granted a foreign-currency retention approval, must be sold to an authorized dealer or deposited into a CBS-authorized foreign-currency account with a licensed bank. A remittance intermediary must therefore settle its offshore float into an authorized foreign-currency account at ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa on a next-business-day basis; any in-country WST conversion required for payouts must be executed through the authorized dealer with a completed exchange-control declaration stating the underlying remittance sender, beneficiary, amount, and purpose.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Clearing Account (USD/AUD/NZD/EUR/GBP) and WST Operational Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (WST) and Correspondent Nostro Clearing Facility
Operational Concentration Account for domestic WST cash-pickup payouts
Secondary settlement account for government-linked and retail beneficiary remittance programs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa has no electronic money institution (EMI), digital-bank, or specialized money-service-business licensing track; the Financial Institutions Act 1996 confines deposit-taking and payment intermediation to licensed banks, and the Exchange Control Act 1976 requires all WST/FX transactions with Samoan counterparties to flow through CBS-authorized dealers. An offshore EMI cannot access the domestic WST clearing grid or hold a CBS settlement account; at best it may operate as a web-sales front end for a licensed Samoan bank, with the bank remaining the settlement principal.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. ANZ and BSP require at least one director and all beneficial owners of the IC and its wholly-owned licensed remittance agent to attend an in-person onboarding interview at an Apia branch, present original passports and proof-of-address, and sign the bank's enhanced due-diligence attestation. Remote opening is not available for high-risk remittance-sector clients; a notarized video-call attestation may supplement, but not replace, the in-person interview unless a board-level waiver is granted by the bank's Group AML Committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IC incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 with nominee shareholders, bearer-share history, or a non-transparent ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents; SIFA Certificate of Good Standing; full register of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs); notarized UBO declarations with passport copies; Tax Exemption Certificate; corporate organizational chart; risk assessment confirming no domestic Samoan business activity by the IC; written undertaking to route all WST retail payouts through a licensed domestic agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Money-transmission activity targeting expatriate corridors with cash-pickup and mobile-wallet touchpoints
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CFT program aligned with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and CBS guidance; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening system specification; customer risk-rating matrix; agent due-diligence and training records; travel-rule integration evidence; sample remittance audit trail from origination to WST payout demonstrating compliance with the 6-month exchange-control repatriation rule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material mismatch between expected settlement velocity and declared equity, indicating unlicensed deposit-taking or money-laundering exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved liquidity and treasury policy; monthly settlement-float reconciliation; committed standby credit facility from an authorized dealer; certified capital introduction via SWIFT MT103 with stated purpose code; CBS authorization for the floating balance; audited financial projections demonstrating that remittance flows are pass-through and never held as deposits beyond the T+1 settlement cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geopolitical exposure of the Chinese-language client acquisition channel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Politically exposed persons (PEP) screening procedure; beneficial-ownership verification of corporate remitters; sanctions overlay covering UN, EU, OFAC, and Samoa consolidated lists; geolocation and IP-integrity controls on the digital channel; independent annual AML audit opinion issued by a Samoan-licensed external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity and subsequent capital support must be transmitted exclusively by SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's or parent treasury's bank account into the IC's designated Capital Escrow Account at ANZ Bank Samoa Limited or BSP Samoa Limited. The wire must carry the stated purpose code 'Equity Contribution' or the applicable exchange-control capital-inflow code under the Exchange Control Regulations 1985, the IC's registration number, and a board resolution attested by the registered agent. CBS prior approval is required where the injected amount is to be converted into WST and retained as domestic working capital; escrowed funds must otherwise remain in the original foreign currency. No cash notes, convertible bearer instruments, or third-party settlements into the escrow account are permissible.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement disbursements use three rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payouts to overseas beneficiary banks and for replenishment of the IC's offshore float; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit and documentary collections issued through ANZ/BSP trade desks for any trade-financed remittance corridors; (3) domestic WST clearances through the CBS interbank settlement system for on-island cash-pickup and account-credit payouts, executed by the licensed domestic remittance agent from its WST settlement account. Every outbound disbursement requires a matched inbound remittance record, an exchange-control declaration, and completed customer due diligence on the beneficiary; the IC shall remain a non-bank intermediary and may never settle directly against the CBS retail payment grid.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright WST/USD, WST/AUD, WST/NZD, and WST/EUR forward contracts with ANZ Samoa, BSP Samoa, or SCB, with tenors up to 12 months matched to forecast remittance payout flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST executed offshore with global counterparties when onshore forward liquidity is insufficient, using the CBS published mid-rate as the fixing source

Cross-currency swaps (WST against USD or AUD) of up to 24 months for structural floating-balance hedging, transacted with an investment-grade correspondent and notified to CBS under exchange-control reporting obligations

Plain-vanilla purchased options on WST (call/put) for contingency hedging of the settlement float, provided the premium is paid from offshore funds and the open option position does not exceed 25% of projected monthly remittance float

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) confirming registered particulars, shareholders, directors, and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, administered through the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (anniversary rule; no calendar-year extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a fixed monetary penalty and suspension of certificate of good standing; continued default for 3 months after written notice authorizes the Registrar to strike off the company with administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Licence Fee / Annual Renewal Fee for continuation of International Company registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable in full on or before 31 January of each calendar year for the current year of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late payment surcharge of 10% of the unpaid fee applies after the due date; non-payment for more than 90 days after written notice permits the Registrar to strike off the company, vest its assets in the Crown, and dissolve it

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Compliance Return and Special Money Transmission Licence Renewal (cross-border remittance rails)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), AML/CFT Supervision Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the licensed company's financial year end (calendar-year filers: due by 31 March); licence is renewable annually effective 1 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual AML return subjects the licensee to a monetary penalty of up to WST 25,000, suspension of the remittance licence, and non-renewal or revocation of the special licence after 90 days

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: International Companies Act 2012 does not impose a general statutory audit; a mandatory independent audit is triggered by (a) a shareholder request holding at least 5% of voting shares, (b) an express director resolution, or (c) the SIFSA special money-transmission licence, which requires audited financial statements annually regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; for licensed remittance entities, SIFSA mandates IFRS-compliant financial statements with no local GAAP variance permitted

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On each annual return, the International Company must confirm that share transfers during the year have been fully recorded in the Register of Members and that the resident registered agent holds current beneficial ownership information; any change of UBO requires the registered agent to file an updated AML/CFT declaration with SIFSA within 14 days, and the annual return must verify that no sanctioned person holds a direct or indirect interest
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 550-1,100 per annum (includes resident registered agent, registered office in Samoa, and prescribed filing services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800-6,500 for a special-purpose licensed remittance audit performed by a certified Samoan public accountant

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987; the standard Samoa resident corporate income tax rate is 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IC status confers a full income tax exemption; the annual Government Fee (approximate WST 400–2,500, depending on share capital) substitutes for income tax; no capital gains tax; no estate duty; no stamp duty on IC share transfers

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return – Form ICA-AR (Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; electronic portal: Samoa Companies Registry)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation of the International Company

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, International Company registration number and registered office address in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact statutory name and certificate number; the registered office must be the physical address of the licensed registered agent, not a P.O. Box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors' and secretary particulars: full legal names, nationality, residential address and passport number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may be listed; nominee directors must also attach the executed deed of nomination and consent to act

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital and shareholder register: total number of issued shares, classes, paid-up capital and names of beneficial shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholders may be natural or legal persons of any nationality; bearer shares must be identified with their custody and title restrictions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity summary: short statement that the IC is engaged in international cross-border remittance facilitation or money transmission services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Avoid indicating any domestic Samoa business or any activity requiring a Samoa domestic banking licence; onshore business by an IC is unlawful

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a daily penalty of WST 25 per day up to a maximum of WST 1,000; failure to file for three consecutive years leads to automatic strike-off and loss of separate legal personality; reinstatement requires a restoration fee plus court order if the limitation period expires

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by an International Company to a non-resident shareholder; the domestic statutory final dividend withholding tax for resident entities is 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because IC dividends are statutorily outside the Samoa tax net, no tax treaty relief is ordinarily required. Should any Samoa-source income be asserted by the Ministry of Revenue, the non-resident shareholder must submit a Form IT10 (Reduced Rate or Exemption Request) together with a certificate of tax residence from the treaty jurisdiction, the dividend board resolution, and supporting share register extracts; the Ministry of Revenue must issue advance approval before repatriation or the withholding agent may be assessed
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Samoa withholding rate on royalties and interest paid by a resident taxable company to a non-resident is 15%. An International Company is generally exempt from such withholding under the International Companies Act 1987. Under Samoa's double taxation agreements, interest and royalty withholding may be reduced to 5–10% where the beneficial owner is entitled to treaty protection and provides a valid TRC

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Samoa transfer-pricing statute is codified for International Companies; for resident companies, the Samoa authorities generally expect OECD-aligned effective transfer-pricing documentation where related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 2,000,000 in annual turnover, including a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: International Companies undertaking relevant banking, financing and leasing activities, cross-border service-centre operations, or pure equity-holding activities are subject to Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations. A cross-border remittance IC must demonstrate in Samoa: board meetings and minutes physically located in Samoa, active direction and control, adequate physical premises, full-time employees commensurate with the activity, and total operating expenditure proportionate to the income. Regulatory guidance distinguishes a genuine remittance-processing company from a shell in tax information-exchange and FATCA/CRS assessments

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through sham offshore characterisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company to carry on actual domestic money-transmission business in Samoa while falsely claiming the IC tax exemption; or failing to declare a Samoa-source operating profit as a resident taxable entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of the full 27% corporate income tax on undeclared Samoa-source profits; addition of a 150% evasion penalty plus statutory interest at 12% per annum; cancellation of the International Company certificate and disqualification of the registered agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the beneficial operator are jointly and severally liable for the taxes and penalties if the company has been stripped of assets; travel bans can be imposed during the investigation; conviction for tax fraud carries imprisonment of up to 15 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no physical presence, no staff, no real board meetings and no records, using the IC solely to interpose a tax-exempt entity between a foreign remittance licence applicant and overseas customers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 10,000 plus WST 100 per day for continued non-compliance; exchange of information with foreign tax authorities under Samoa's competent-authority arrangements; the IC may be struck off and its bank accounts frozen
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced; directors become personally liable for the underlying penalties and foreign tax assessments; courts can issue a restitution order against the directors and impose a five-year bar on serving as a director in Samoa or a major financial centre

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cross-border remittance rails, Swift-based payout settlement, or cash-pickup clearing service without a Samoa money transmitter or banking licence from the Samoa Central Bank and without AML/CFT measures, KYC records and transaction monitoring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Licence refusal or revocation; mandatory winding-up of the entity; asset freezing and forfeiture; administrative fines up to WST 500,000 or 5% of the transaction volume in Samoa, whichever is higher; referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit for money-laundering prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior compliance officers are personally liable for civil penalties and are disqualified from holding any financial-services licence; deliberate participation in money laundering attracts criminal imprisonment of up to 10 years and extradition under mutual legal assistance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-border regulatory evasion in destination markets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing expatriate money-transfer services to consumers in the United States or other high-regulation markets without registering the Samoa IC as a money services business with the relevant supervisory authority, or failing to disclose the IC as the effective service provider
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa has no extra-territorial criminal sanction, but foreign regulators may issue cease-and-desist orders, asset freezes and restitution to consumers; correspondent banking access may be severed, FATF listing risk increases, and Samoa's regulator may order license revocation of the paying agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face foreign criminal prosecution, including U.S. charges for unlicensed money transmission under 18 U.S.C. § 1960, leading to imprisonment of up to 5 years per count, criminal forfeiture, and personal fines; travel to the enforcing jurisdiction is restricted and extradition may be sought

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misleading statutory records and concealment of beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing false director or shareholder particulars, failing to maintain the registered office and records in Samoa, concealing the true beneficial owner behind a nominee without executing the required declarations, or destroying records relevant to a cross-border transaction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of WST 5,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; strike-off and dissolution of the IC; revocation of the registered agent's licence; public insolvency examination if the entity cannot pay claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and severally liable for all company debts where the company has traded while insolvent or has acted upon unauthorised instructions; the court may order civil restitution, freeze personal assets, impose a travel ban, and commit the directors to prison for criminal contempt
